tensor.d: A grid of numbers with any number of axes (0 = scalar, 1 = vector, 2 = matrix, 3+ = tensor proper). In memory it is a pointer + type + shape + strides + offset.

vetor.d: An ordered list of \(d\) numbers, which can also be read as an arrow in a \(d\)-dimensional space: the direction says “what”, the length says “how much”. Every token in an LLM is a vector of hidden_size numbers.

hidden-size.d: Width of the vector each token carries through the residual stream: 4096 in GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 2560 in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. It is the \(K\) of almost every decode GEMM.

produto-escalar.d: \( \mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b = \sum_i a_i b_i = \lVert\mathbf a\rVert\lVert\mathbf b\rVert\cos\theta \): multiply coordinate by coordinate and add up. It measures alignment; it is the math behind the logits, the attention scores, the routers and every output of a linear layer.

similaridade-cosseno.d: \( \cos(\mathbf a,\mathbf b) = \mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b / (\lVert\mathbf a\rVert\,\lVert\mathbf b\rVert) \in [-1, 1] \): the dot product without the influence of the lengths. 1 = same direction, 0 = orthogonal, −1 = opposite.

norma-l2.d: Length of a vector: \( \lVert\mathbf x\rVert_2 = \sqrt{\sum_i x_i^2} \) (Pythagoras in \(d\) dimensions). It grows with \(d\) even if each coordinate has a fixed typical size.

norma-rms.d: \( \operatorname{RMS}(\mathbf x) = \sqrt{\tfrac1d\sum_i x_i^2} = \lVert\mathbf x\rVert_2/\sqrt d \): the typical size of a coordinate, independent of \(d\). It is the denominator of RMSNorm.

concentracao-de-medida.d: In high dimension, almost all randomly drawn directions are nearly orthogonal: the cosine between two of them has a spread of ~\(1/\sqrt d\) (≈ 0.016 at d = 4096). It explains why many nearly independent directions fit and why random rotations spread out outliers.

matriz.d: An \(m\times n\) table of numbers that represents a linear function from \(\mathbb R^n\) to \(\mathbb R^m\): \( \mathbf y = W\mathbf x \). Each row is a direction detector; each column is the image of an axis.

transformacao-linear.d: A function that respects sums and multiples: \( W(\alpha\mathbf a + \beta\mathbf b) = \alpha W\mathbf a + \beta W\mathbf b \). It keeps the origin fixed, maps lines to lines and evenly spaced grids to evenly spaced grids. Every matrix is one, and every one can be written as a matrix.

determinante.d: The factor by which a square matrix multiplies areas (or volumes). Negative when it mirrors space; zero when it flattens a dimension (the matrix has no inverse).

posto.d: The number of independent directions a matrix produces: the dimension of its image, equal to the number of linearly independent columns (or rows). Not to be confused with a tensor's ndim or with a GPU's process rank.

canal-de-saida.d: In a PyTorch weight [out, in], an output channel is a row (one neuron) and an input channel is a column. A “per-channel” scale = one scale per row; a “per-token” scale = one per row of the activation.

pesos-e-ativacoes.d: Weights: fixed, learned numbers, stored in memory and read at every step. Activations: numbers that change with every token and are born during the computation. In a GEMM \(Y = XW\), \(X\) holds the activations \([M, K]\) and \(W\) the weights \([K, N]\).

gemm.d: General matrix multiply: \( Y_{[M\times N]} = X_{[M\times K]}\,W_{[K\times N]} \), costing \(2MNK\) FLOPs. Each weight is reused \(M\) times, once per row of \(X\). It is the operation that dominates an LLM's time.

gemv.d: Multiplying a weight matrix by a single activation vector (a GEMM with \(M = 1\)). Each weight read from memory serves a single operation: the arithmetic intensity sits at ~1 FLOP/B in BF16, and the time is the time to read the weights. It is the typical math of decode with one sequence.

flops.d: Number of floating-point operations in a computation. A GEMM costs \(2MNK\) (one multiplication and one addition per term). Rule of thumb: a forward pass costs ~2 × active parameters FLOPs per token. Not to be confused with FLOPS (per second), the measure of GPU speed.

cublas.d: NVIDIA's dense linear algebra library for GPUs: ready-made, highly optimized GEMMs in BF16, FP16, FP8 and more. In the GLM recipe, it is the BF16 path the KDA input projection uses when \(M > 512\) (prefill).

shape.d: The tuple with the size of each axis of a tensor, such as [T, 4, 4096]; the number of axes is the ndim. A linear layer only sees the last axis: […, K] → […, N].

reshape.d: Reinterpreting the same elements with another shape, for example [T, H·dₕ] → [T, H, dₕ]. When the strides allow it, nothing is copied (it is a view); otherwise, reshape has to copy.

transposicao.d: Swapping two axes (\(A^\top_{ij} = A_{ji}\)). In PyTorch it is a view: the strides swap places and no byte moves, but the tensor is no longer contiguous.

projecao-fundida.d: Several matrices that take the same input, concatenated along the output so that a single GEMM runs and the result is split afterwards. E.g.: the KDA in_proj_qkvbfg_a in GLM merges q, k, v, β and the down-projections of the two gates: [12576 × 4096] per GPU at TP=2.

broadcasting.d: The rule that combines tensors of different shapes: it aligns the shapes from the right and, on each axis, requires equal sizes or one of them equal to 1 (which is virtually repeated, with stride 0). E.g.: bias [N] + activation [M, N].

einsum.d: A notation that gives a letter to each axis: letters from the inputs that do not appear in the output are summed. 'mk,kn->mn' is a GEMM; 'i,j->ij' is an outer product; 'bsgd,grd->bsgr' is DeepSeek-V4's grouped output.

stride.d: How many elements to skip in memory to move one position along an axis. Address = base + (offset + Σ index·stride) × itemsize. A contiguous [3, 4] tensor has strides (4, 1); transposed, sliced, expanded or as_strided views have others, and kernels that assume a dense layout address them wrong.

contiguo.d: A tensor whose elements sit in memory exactly in logical order (last axis with stride 1, each earlier axis skipping the product of the following ones). .contiguous() copies into this layout when needed.

view-tensor.d: A tensor that shares another's memory, with a different shape, strides or offset: transposes, slices, expands and compatible reshapes. It copies no data, and writing to a view changes the original.

as-strided.d: Creates a view with a hand-picked shape and strides over an existing block of memory. vLLM uses views like this to fit several logical tensors into the same KV allocation; GLM's kpool tail is one of them, with stride(0) = a whole indexer page.

baixo-posto.d: Writing (or approximating) an \(m\times n\) matrix as the product \(AB\) of two thin ones, \(A\,(m\times r)\) and \(B\,(r\times n)\): \(r(m+n)\) numbers instead of \(mn\), and the input passes through an \(r\)-dimensional bottleneck. It is the basis of MLA, LoRA, the KDA gates and the Markov head.

svd.d: \( W = U\Sigma V^\top \): every matrix is a rotation, a per-axis stretch (the singular values) and another rotation. Keeping the \(r\) largest singular values gives the best rank-\(r\) approximation (Eckart–Young).

matriz-ortogonal.d: A matrix with \(Q^\top Q = I\): unit-length, mutually perpendicular columns. It preserves dot products, lengths and angles; its inverse is its transpose. \(\det = +1\) is a rotation, \(-1\) a reflection. E.g.: RoPE and Hadamard.

rotacao.d: An orthogonal matrix with determinant +1. In the plane, \(R(\theta)\) rotates by \(\theta\), and \(R(\alpha)R(\beta) = R(\alpha+\beta)\), \(R(\theta)^\top = R(-\theta)\). RoPE applies position-dependent rotations to pairs of dimensions.

projecao-ortogonal.d: \( P_\alpha = I - \alpha\,\hat{\mathbf r}\hat{\mathbf r}^\top \) multiplies the component along \(\hat{\mathbf r}\) by \(1-\alpha\) and leaves the rest alone: α = 1 removes the direction (orthogonal projection, no inverse), α = 2 mirrors (Householder), α > 1 over-projects. The proj method of GLM's abliteration uses α = 3 (also written λ in some texts).

intensidade-aritmetica.d: FLOPs executed per byte read from memory. For a GEMM with \(M \ll K, N\), \(I \approx 2M/b_w\) (≈ \(M\) in BF16). Compared with the GPU's ridge (~458 FLOP/B on the GB10, BF16), it tells you whether the kernel is memory-bound or compute-bound.

ridge-point.d: The ratio between peak compute and memory bandwidth, \(P/B\). On the GB10: ~125 TFLOPS BF16 / ~273 GB/s ≈ 458 FLOP/B. Below this intensity, the kernel waits for memory; above it, it waits for the cores.

memory-bound.d: A kernel whose time is dominated by reading and writing bytes: the cores wait for the data. It is the regime of GEMMs with small \(M\), such as decode: processing 32 rows costs almost the same as 1.

compute-bound.d: A kernel whose time is dominated by the arithmetic operations, with intensity above the ridge. It is the regime of prefill, with thousands of rows per GEMM.
